title: Book 6 — Erato, Chapter 44
paragraphs: These cities, I say, furnished them with a pretext for the expedition; but they had it in mind to subdue as many of the Hellenic cities as they could. First they subdued with their ships the Thasians, who did not even raise a hand to defend themselves; then with the land-army they added the Macedonians to the peoples already serving them—for all the nations east of the Macedonians had already before this become subject to them. Crossing over then from Thasos to the opposite coast, they continued their way close to land as far as Acanthus, and then, starting from Acanthus, they attempted to round Mount Athos. But as they sailed round, there fell upon them a violent north wind against which they could do nothing; it handled them very roughly, dashing very many of their ships onto Mount Athos. It is said in fact that the number of ships destroyed was three hundred, and more than twenty thousand men; for since the sea around Athos is very full of sea monsters, some of the men were seized by these and so perished, while others were dashed against the rocks; some of them did not know how to swim and perished for that reason, others again from cold.
